title: Grove selects CLOs as a first credit allocation partly to establish a reusable model for offchain credit under onchain governance
content:
A.6.1.1.2.3.2.1 states that "Grove will prioritize Collateralized Loan Obligations (CLOs) as the initial pathway to provide Sky ecosystem with rapid exposure to higher yielding investment-grade credit assets, **establishing a scalable model for offchain credit with onchain governance**."

Two justifications are given, and the second is the durable one. The first is about the asset — CLOs offer investment-grade credit at attractive yields and can be accessed quickly. The second is about the *process*: doing a CLO requires solving how an onchain governance system executes and oversees an offchain credit transaction, and that solution is reusable for every subsequent one.

So the first deal's return is not the whole of its value. The legal entity structure, the authorization route, the custody arrangements and the reporting path all have to be built once and can then be reused. A.6.1.1.2.3.6.7 shows this being concretized: a DAO Resolution authorizing the Grove Foundation and **Cedar Grove Ltd** to subscribe for and purchase Class B notes issued by Galaxy CLO 2025-1 LLC — a distinct legal entity for the CLO exposure, separate from the entities used for the exchange and stablecoin relationships.

The framing has a specific implication for evaluation. A pathfinder allocation should be judged on whether the pathway it built is reusable, not only on how the notes perform, and it justifies a smaller, more conservative first transaction than the yield alone would warrant.

It also identifies where the real risk sits. If the model is the product, then a defect in the template — in how authorization, custody or valuation is structured — propagates to every allocation built on it, which is a different and more consequential failure than one CLO underperforming.
description: A.6.1.1.2.3.2.1 frames CLOs as the pathway to rapid investment-grade exposure and as a scalable template, so the initial transaction is infrastructure as much as investment.
